title: A Border for the Deadline
premise: Kestrel Reyes, a ghost-hired interpreter for a doomed peace delegation in the border city of Vellmar, is the only person who remembers Flight 447 landing—because she was its last passenger before every record of it erased itself mid-air. Hunting the truth pulls her into an alliance with Ilya Marchetti, the delegation's disgraced security chief, and a found family of records-clerk dissidents who traffic in unattributable truths. As the delegation collapses and both governments move to bury the flight's cargo—a witness list to an atrocity both sides committed—Kestrel must choose between publishing the list and trading it for the lives of her new family. In the end she trades it, but secretly keeps one name: her own mother's, discovering the erasure was built to protect her all along.
about_author: Mara Zhou spent six years working as a contract interpreter for diplomatic missions across three continents, where she learned that the most dangerous sentences are the ones no one will admit were spoken. She writes thrillers about people whose professions require them to be forgettable.

chapters.title: The Language of No One
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She interprets a hostile preliminary session of the Vellmar peace delegation, deliberately flattening a threat into bureaucratic mush to keep both sides talking. Establishes her craft of strategic invisibility and her rule: never be the story. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Flight 447
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Taking an unscheduled red-eye home from a side assignment, she shares a tense conversation with a nervous man clutching a leather folio. He presses a slip of paper into her hand as they land: a single name. Emotional beat: unease she can't yet name.

chapters.title: No Such Flight
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The airline has no record of her ticket; the airport manifest shows an empty slot; even her own boarding pass photo won't load. The nervous man from the plane is found dead in the river, ruled a drowning days before the flight landed. Emotional beat: vertigo—the ground truth of reality shifting.

chapters.title: The Man Who Counts Doors
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Security chief Ilya Marchetti notices Kestrel asking quiet questions and recognizes the look of someone being hunted—he was trained to spot it. He warns her off, then follows her anyway. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity hardening into protectiveness.

chapters.title: Found Family
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Following the name on the slip, she finds the Annex, an archive squat run by former records clerks—Odile, Tam, and young Prew—who preserve documents both governments erase. They confirm Flight 447 existed. Emotional beat: the startling warmth of being believed.

chapters.title: What the Delegation Was For
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Ilya discovers the peace talks are theater; both delegations have pre-drafted identical failure statements dated weeks ahead. Someone needs the talks to collapse on schedule. Emotional beat: disillusionment curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: The Folio
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Reconstructing the dead man's identity, she learns he was a courier for the Witness List—names documenting an atrocity committed jointly by both sides during the border war. The flight's erasure wasn't about the plane; it was about what left it. Emotional beat: horror with a purpose.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Ilya catches surveillance on Kestrel and burns his first professional line by intervening, officially going rogue. Their uneasy partnership forms over a diner table, trading half-truths. Emotional beat: two lonely professionals choosing trust as an act of defiance.

chapters.title: Erasure Protocol
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The Annex is raided; Odile is taken, and the archive burns. But Prew had already smuggled out the core index. Kestrel realizes the enemy can edit records but not memories—and that she is now the only living index. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into responsibility.

chapters.title: The Interpreter's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A flashback chapter: how Kestrel learned years ago that a mistranslation she was ordered to make cost lives, and why she vowed never again to be the invisible instrument of someone else's violence. Emotional beat: the wound that drives everything.

chapters.title: Negotiating with Ghosts
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Ilya identifies the erasure operation's handler: Deputy Minister Corvane, his old mentor, who offers Ilya reinstatement in exchange for delivering Kestrel and the list. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: Nine Names
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Decoding the courier's index, the team finds nine names on the Witness List remain findable; eight are already dead or erased. The ninth is a woman living under a changed name in the port district—one Kestrel recognizes from a photograph she's carried since childhood. Emotional beat: dread blooming into recognition.

chapters.title: Mother Tongue
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel confronts the ninth name: Elena Reyes, her mother, who didn't abandon her twenty years ago but went into hiding after testifying about the atrocity. Her mother's disappearance and Kestrel's career of invisibility were the same survival strategy. Emotional beat: fury and love colliding.

chapters.title: The Deadline
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. The delegation's final session is set; Corvane plans to close the talks, declare the past settled, and complete the erasures within seventy-two hours. Ilya learns Kestrel's mother is the last loose end. Emotional beat: the clock becoming audible.

chapters.title: Safe House Sonata
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Hiding with her mother, Prew, and Ilya in a port safe house, Kestrel experiences the family she never had—shared meals, watch rotations, Prew teaching Elena encryption games. For one evening, the thriller pauses. Emotional beat: fragile domestic joy under siege.

chapters.title: Betrayal Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Corvane's people trace them; someone inside the network leaked. Evidence points to Tam, but Ilya deduces the real leak is the Annex's own dead-drop protocol, compromised long ago. Tam flees anyway, wounded by suspicion. Emotional beat: trust fracturing under pressure.

chapters.title: The Trade
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Cornered, Kestrel makes the offer she swore she'd never make: the Witness List in exchange for amnesty for her mother, Prew, and Tam. Corvane accepts—but demands Ilya deliver it personally, ensuring his complicity. Emotional beat: sacrifice disguised as surrender.

chapters.title: Session Final
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. At the closing plenary, Ilya hands over the list while interpreting Kestrel's whispered translation of the joint statement—she embeds a coded phrase only the Annex would recognize, signaling the trade happened under duress. Emotional beat: the climax's cold ceremony.

chapters.title: What Erasure Cannot Touch
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The exchange completes; her family walks free. But Kestrel reveals she memorized the entire list verbatim—an interpreter's gift—and has already begun dictating it to Prew's distributed network. Erasing paper was never enough. Emotional beat: quiet triumph.

chapters.title: Corvane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Ilya confronts Corvane privately, not with violence but with the knowledge that the list survives in forty scattered heads. Corvane's power depends on a silence that no longer exists. The old mentor stands down. Emotional beat: victory without vengeance.

chapters.title: A Border for the Deadline
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The delegation fails exactly on schedule, but the failure statement now circulates alongside fragments of the truth. Kestrel crosses the border legally for the first time, her mother beside her, no longer invisible by force but private by choice. Emotional beat: release.

chapters.title: The One Name Kept
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, epilogue. Months later, running a small language school above the rebuilt Annex, Kestrel opens her mother's original testimony and finds the final entry: a clause protecting 'the interpreter's daughter'—the erasure was partly built to shield her. She closes the file, keeps the secret, and answers the door to a new student. Emotional beat: peace earned, not given.
